page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-64 is a compute-focused instance within the first-generation N1 machine family. It provides 64 vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading on 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon processors using the x86_64 architecture. The system is provisioned with 58.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, though modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX are not present. The configuration does not include local disk storage or bundled GPUs, requiring all persistence to be handled via attached network storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing capabilities alongside modest single-thread metrics. Multi-threaded evaluations such as stress-ng multi-core reached 47,081.36 and Geekbench multi-core achieved 9,980.0, placing the instance in the middle tier of comparable cloud hardware. In contrast, single-core benchmarks, including Geekbench single-core at 948.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1,116.79, fall into the lower quartile due to the older base architecture and moderate clock frequency. Memory bandwidth reaches 77.81 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 32.34 GB/sec for writes. Workload tests reflect consistent parallel throughput, delivering 41.94 million Redis SET operations per second and 26.36 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Cost efficiency for this instance is rooted in its high vCPU density relative to memory capacity, minimizing expenditures on unused RAM for CPU-bound tasks. However, the presence of older CPU cores limits execution speed per thread compared to newer hardware generations. The configuration is suitable for distributed batch processing, parallel compilation tasks, scale-out web serving fleets, and high-concurrency microservices that require substantial core counts without extensive per-thread memory demands.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-64 is a compute-oriented virtual machine designed for multi-threaded workloads requiring high CPU core density. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, it delivers 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores alongside 58.0 GB of memory, yielding roughly 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance lacks local storage and discrete GPUs, relying on networked block storage for persistence. In performance testing, multi-threaded metrics such as Geekbench multi-core (9,980.0) and stress-ng multi-core (47,081.36) demonstrate balanced throughput across parallel workloads. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into the bottom tier due to legacy architecture and modest clock rates. Featuring AVX and AES instructions, the n1-highcpu-64 is well suited for parallel software compilation, static web serving, containerized application clusters, and distributed batch processing.
